## `inventory-transfer post`

Move stock from one inventory site to another, as the anchor's Transfer Inventory does: from_site, to_site and 1-200 lines (item and quantity in its base unit), with date (default today), memo and reason. Each line takes the quantity out of the from site and puts it in the to site on that date. Nothing is posted: no journal entry, no value and no cost change, because an item has one average cost company-wide. Stock leaves and arrives at once (nothing is held in transit). Taking the from site below zero is saved with a warning that names where else the item is. A date on or before the closing date is refused. The result gives the transfer number and each site's on hand after it. Moving money between accounts is `transfer post`. Example: `bookflow inventory-transfer post --from-site "Van 1" --to-site Warehouse --lines '[{"item":"Widget","quantity":"5"}]' --reason "Unloaded 5 widgets from the van"`.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Feature | — |

| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow inventory-transfer post --from-site "Van 1" --to-site Warehouse --lines '[{"item":"Widget","quantity":"5"}]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Unloaded 5 widgets from the van" --json`


## `inventory-transfer update`

Correct a transfer under its expected version: name only what changes (date, sites, lines, memo). The old placements are reversed and the new ones written in one transaction; nothing is posted. An update reaching a date on or before the closing date is refused.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/inventory-transfer.update` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow inventory-transfer update T-1 --expected-version 1 --lines '[{"item":"Widget","quantity":"4"}]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Only four came off" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "inventory-transfer update", "input": {"transfer": "T-1", "expected_version": 1, "lines": [{"item": "Widget", "quantity": "4"}]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `transfer` | `TRANSFER` | string | yes | no | — | Transfer ID or number.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer | yes | no | — | The transfer version this change was decided from.; minimum 1 |
| `date` | `--date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `from_site` | `--from-site` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `to_site` | `--to-site` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `lines[].item` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Inventory part or assembly to move, by id or name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `lines[].quantity` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Quantity to move in the item base unit, a positive decimal.; minimum length 1; maximum length 40 |
| `lines[].description` | inside `--lines` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `count_position` | `--count-position` | literal["before", "after"] \| null | no | yes | null | — |

### Command and context options

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/inventory-transfer.update`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

## `inventory-transfer void`

Void a transfer, with a reason: its stock goes back to the sites it came from. A void is final and kept in history. Refused when the transfer is dated on or before the closing date.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.
